title: Foundational Challenges in Assuring Alignment and Safety of Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: As a survey and research agenda, the paper reviews existing methodologies for evaluating gender bias, such as analyzing stereotypical biases during translation into languages with different pronoun structures (e.g., Bengali, Farsi, Turkish) and observing biased outputs in simulated complex tasks like writing reference letters or screening resumes.
The paper discusses evaluating racial bias by testing models in complex, real-world downstream scenarios, such as recruitment and resume screening, rather than just simple prompt evaluations.

The paper reviews evaluations that compare LLM responses on cognitive psychological tasks and value surveys to human responses across different demographics, noting that models disproportionately reflect Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic (WEIRD) societies and underrepresent the Global South.

The paper surveys methodologies that evaluate bias toward particular political ideologies, including prompting models to take on specific personas or testing their responses to morally ambiguous and politically contentious situations (e.g., gun control).

The paper discusses evaluating language bias by comparing model performance, factual accuracy, and safety constraint adherence (e.g., jailbreak success rates) across high-resource languages, low-resource languages, and dialects used by marginalized groups.

The paper reviews evaluations of biases in LLM-based automated evaluation systems, such as measuring position biases, verbosity biases (preference for longer answers), and egocentric biases (preference for the model's own outputs) when scoring texts.
